title: Grateful Dead Live at Hartford Civic Center on 1982-04-17

ai_review.summary: A solid soundboard capture of a high‑energy 4/17/82 Hartford show, highlighted by a smoking Shakedown, Lost Sailor→Saint, soaring Uncle John’s Band and an emotional Baby Blue encore.
ai_review.review: The recording is a mostly clean SBD (with a brief audience patch early in Sugaree) that delivers clear vocals and well‑balanced instruments, though it isn’t as crisp as some other ’82 tapes. Musically the concert shines – the second set flows like an “express train” with a thunderous Shakedown, a rare Lost Sailor>Saint, a sublime Uncle John’s Band rising out of space, a tight Not Fade Away and a monster Baby Blue that showcases Jerry’s vocal peak. Overall the performance is high‑energy, tightly played, and consistently praised by reviewers.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviews (≈70%) are 4–5 stars praising both the music and the soundboard quality; weighted rating (70 % show, 30 % recording) yields a strong overall score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear SBD after ~3 min into Sugaree; early portion is an audience (AUD/FOB) patch, some reviewers note slight echo‑yness and less crispness than top‑tier ’82 tapes but overall balanced and listenable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Second set described as a seamless ‘express train’ with no dead time, strong transitions from space into Uncle John’s and into the encore; first set solid but less remarkable.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for playful riff trades with Brent, crisp guitar tone, ripping runs on Sailor>Saint, powerful vocal delivery on Baby Blue and Sugaree (fanning mode).
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted goofing behind Bob during Lost Sailor and providing solid bass foundation; occasional “Phil bombs” comments but no detailed critiques.
band_member_comments.Bob: Vocals highlighted as passionate on Around & Around/OMSN, strong lead on Baby Blue, and generally praised for his presence in the set.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent Mydland’s keyboards described as trippy, massive jam‑fuel during Shakedown, subtle color shifts throughout; many reviewers single him out for his performance.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drum space called remarkable and “beautiful” leading into Uncle John’s; overall drum work deemed solid though not overly heavy.
